cases.title: Two-repo suite from a non-repo folder applies to both repos
steps: Build as TESTING.md describes (npm run build)
Create two temp git repos A and B and a plain temp folder H (not a repo)
Add a task folder and PRD to A (feature fa) and to B (feature fb) with the fake-provider fixtures, commit both
From H run node dist/cli.js suite --feature A/fa:A/PRD-fa.md --feature B/fb:B/PRD-fb.md --provider fake
cases.expected: Exit code 0; H/.graph-execution/suite-<id>/suite.json has status applied and 2 entries in repos; A shows only fa's files and B only fb's files as uncommitted changes; suite/<id> exists in both repos

cases.title: One repo that cannot take its result blocks every apply
steps: Set up A, B and H as in P1
After committing, switch B to a new branch other
Run the same suite command from H
cases.expected: Nothing is applied in A or B (git status clean in both); the suite log contains 'b: not applying' naming the checkout branch, and 'nothing applied'; both results stay on suite/<id>

cases.title: Each repo validates with its own commands
steps: Set up as P1, and commit in A graph-execution.config.json {"validate":["test -f a1.txt"],"validateAt":"end"} and in B {"validate":["test -f b1.txt"],"validateAt":"end"} (task ids a1 and b1)
Run the suite from H
cases.expected: Exit code 0 and both repos applied, which requires each command to run only in its own repo's worktree

cases.title: An e2e fixer change lands only in its repo
steps: Set up as P1
Write a fake script (GRAPH_EXECUTION_FAKE_SCRIPT) where the e2e code reviewer reports one major finding in round 0 and the e2e fixer writes b/fix.txt
Run the suite from H with --no-merge
cases.expected: B's suite/<id> has a commit adding fix.txt after the merge commits; A's suite/<id> has no commit after its merges

cases.title: Single-repo suite is unchanged
steps: Create one temp repo A with two features, commit
Run node dist/cli.js suite --feature ... --feature ... --provider fake from inside A
cases.expected: Exit code 0, status applied, suite folder in A/.graph-execution, integration worktree path was worktrees/integration, repos has one entry, the log has no repo-name prefixes

cases.title: clean in a non-home repo spares a live suite
steps: Start a two-repo suite from H whose fb task hangs (fake script {"task:b1":{"attempts":[{"hang":true}]}}) with --web
While it runs, run node dist/cli.js clean --done inside A, then node dist/cli.js list inside A
cases.expected: No suite/<id> or graph/<run-id> branch of the live suite is deleted in A; A/.graph-execution/_suites/<suite-id>.json exists

cases.title: Missing repo: resume fails, clean still cleans
steps: Run a two-repo suite from H that ends failed (a feature fails all attempts)
Move B away
From H run node dist/cli.js suite --resume, then node dist/cli.js clean <suite-id>
cases.expected: --resume exits non-zero with 'repo <B path> not found'; clean warns 'repo <B path> not found; skipped', deletes A's suite branches and the suite folder

cases.title: Suite page groups features by repo
steps: Run a two-repo suite from H with --web (TESTING.md shows how to open and inspect the page with a browser)
Open the page
cases.expected: Feature boxes appear under a label per repo name; the apply node reads 'apply → 2 repos'; opening a file of the apply node shows its diff with a repo-prefixed path
